currentContext.business: PPAP manufactures automotive body sealing systems, injection-molded plastic components and engineered polymer products for leading passenger vehicle OEMs across India, using plastic extrusion, plastic injection molding, rubber processing and advanced manufacturing technologies. Its components are compatible with both internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric vehicle (EV) platforms, making the portfolio largely engine-agnostic. Around the core automotive parts business the Group has added an aftermarket distribution business (ELPIS), a commercial tooling vertical, an industrial products business (Avinya Industrial Products) and a lithium-ion battery pack business (Avinya Batteries).

Industrial Products: components for solar panel cleaning robots

battery packs for solar energy systems, telecom infrastructure, Energy Storage Systems (ESS), inverters and UPS

currentContext.strengths: Over four decades of experience in engineering and manufacturing as the flagship of the AJAY Group|Engine-agnostic product portfolio compatible with both ICE and EV platforms, making it future-ready|Manufacturing network located close to major automotive production hubs across Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra, supported by 7 manufacturing facilities at Group level|Operating scale — daily dispatches exceeding 2.3 lakh parts, over 50 customers and a portfolio of 3000+ SKUs|Diversified blue-chip customer base including Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors and Honda, with Mahindra & Mahindra onboarded as a direct OEM customer and CIE Golde as a direct Tier-I customer in FY26|Technical collaboration with Nissen Chemitec Corporation, Japan, and a technology partnership agreement with Hutchinson entered in June 2026 giving access to European body-sealing technology and licensed knowhow|In-house precision tooling capability (multi-cavity, gas-assisted, hot runner, 2K and over-moulding) supporting new product development|Core process capabilities spanning plastic extrusion, plastic injection molding and rubber processing, transferable to non-automotive industrial applications
currentContext.strategies: Build the AJAY Group as a diversified enterprise around the automotive parts core, with five companies each addressing a distinct segment of the mobility and industrial value chain — automotive components, aftermarket, industrial products, precision tooling and energy storage.|Simplify the group structure: complete the divestment of the PPAP Tokai India Rubber Private Limited stake, transfer the tooling business into wholly owned subsidiary Meraki Precision Tool Engineering Limited during FY27, and merge Avinya Batteries Limited into PPAP.|Keep the automotive product portfolio engine-agnostic so it serves both ICE and EV platforms, and raise content per vehicle by introducing value-added components.|Expand and re-lay out the manufacturing footprint — re-layout of Pathredi, Gujarat and Chennai plants with a solar plant, commissioning of a new EPDM extrusion line and second mixing line at the new Chennai facility, and new facilities at Sambhaji Nagar and Chakan, Pune, for capacity growth and customer proximity.|Broaden the OEM customer base and deepen key programs — Mahindra & Mahindra onboarded as a direct OEM customer and CIE Golde as a direct Tier-I customer, with launch readiness for Tata Motors, Mahindra, Honda and Maruti Suzuki programs.|Scale the aftermarket business through a pan-India distribution network backed by regional warehouses, an omnichannel/digital commerce presence, premium and value-added offerings, and direct exports.|Grow the tooling vertical towards complex, high-value moulds (multi-cavity, 2K, over-molding) to improve margins, expand export capability, and invest in high-speed machining, automation and advanced CAD/CAM.|Diversify beyond automotive through Avinya Industrial Products, using plastic extrusion, rubber extrusion and injection moulding capability to expand into industrial and export markets and create a more diversified revenue base.|Access external technology — technical collaboration with Nissen Chemitec Corporation, Japan, and a technology partnership agreement with Hutchinson (June 2026) to manufacture advanced body sealing systems in India for the passenger vehicle segment.
currentContext.expansion: PPAP's stated expansion agenda for the automotive parts business covers work at the Pathredi, Gujarat and Chennai manufacturing facilities to enhance operational efficiency, optimize production flow and improve capacity utilization, together with the set-up of a solar plant for energy efficiency; commissioning of a new EPDM extrusion line and a second mixing line at the new Chennai facility; and expansion of the manufacturing footprint through new facilities at Sambhaji Nagar and Chakan, Pune, to support capacity growth and customer proximity. The product portfolio is to be widened with value-added components to raise content per vehicle. In the aftermarket business (ELPIS Automotives Private Limited) the build-out is distribution-led — a pan-India network supported by regional warehouses, an omnichannel/digital commerce presence and direct exports to the Middle East, Africa and South Asia. The tooling business, run from the Greater Noida facility, is to receive continued investment in high-speed machining, automation and advanced CAD/CAM systems, and is proposed to be transferred into a dedicated wholly owned subsidiary, Meraki Precision Tool Engineering Limited, during FY27 subject to statutory and regulatory approvals. The industrial products business, which has a facility in Surajpur, Uttar Pradesh, established an additional facility at Greater Noida during FY26 to improve customer proximity and delivery responsiveness. In batteries, growth is to be driven through prismatic line capacity expansion, and Avinya Batteries Limited is proposed to be merged into PPAP Automotive Limited, subject to the requisite statutory and regulatory approvals, with the merger expected to complete during FY27. No rupee capex quantum is disclosed in this material: the Capital Commitments and Segment Capital Expenditure named-disclosure blocks arrive with their labels only and carry no attributable figure.
currentContext.mdna: India's auto component industry is expected to grow at a 7-8% CAGR between FY25 and FY30, supported by robust domestic demand, rising exports, favourable policy and technological advancement.|Record Indian automobile sales in FY26 across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, three-wheelers and two-wheelers, plus record vehicle exports, are expected to support demand for automotive components and related industries.|Electrification, smartification, premiumization and localization are the key trends driving component demand, with the mix shifting towards high-value products such as battery systems and electric powertrains.|Government programmes — the PLI Scheme, Make in India, FAME and PM E-Drive — are accelerating EV adoption and domestic manufacturing of advanced automotive components.|Favourable demographics, rising vehicle ownership and continued growth in domestic manufacturing support a positive long-term industry outlook.|A growing aftermarket, India's growing vehicle parc and rising average vehicle age underpin demand for replacement parts and accessories.|Rising premium vehicle penetration supports demand for higher-value sealing, plastic and aesthetic components.|Management flags geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain disruptions, commodity price volatility and evolving regulatory requirements as the key risks to this demand outlook.|Automotive parts: secured new business wins worth approximately Rs 840 crore across both EV and ICE vehicle platforms in FY26.|Automotive parts: new projects started for Tata Motors Sierra, MSIL E Vitara & Victoris and Renault-Nissan Duster, with launch readiness under development for Tata Motors, Mahindra, Honda and Maruti Suzuki programs.|Tooling: maintained a robust order pipeline across automotive and non-automotive sectors, supporting future growth; the stated priority is to maintain a strong order pipeline to provide sustained revenue visibility.|Tooling: 148 precision molds developed and delivered in FY26, with capacity utilisation improving to over 90%.

risks.note: Demand for automotive components remains closely linked to vehicle production volumes, which can be affected by economic slowdowns and consumer sentiment — and the automotive parts business remains the Company's core growth engine and largest revenue contributor.

Geopolitical developments, logistics constraints and global trade uncertainties may affect production schedules and costs. The BRSR materiality table rates supply chain disruption as a negative-implication risk that, if unmanaged, could adversely affect production volume, revenue, profitability, customer satisfaction and reputation; mitigation is a supply chain risk management framework with early, proactive supplier engagement.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and inflation
risks.note: The Company states it is exposed to risks arising from fluctuations in raw material prices and inflationary pressures, which may impact profitability — relevant given FY26 gross margin gains were attributed to product mix and raw material cost efficiencies.

risks.risk: OEM customer power and continuous cost-down pressure
risks.note: As a preferred supplier to leading automotive OEMs, maintaining stringent quality standards, timely delivery and cost optimisation is critical to sustaining long-term customer relationships; increasing customer expectations for cost reduction and product development necessitate ongoing investment in manufacturing excellence, automation and process improvements.

risks.risk: Rising ESG, safety and sustainability compliance burden
risks.note: The automotive component industry is witnessing heightened compliance requirements relating to environmental, social, governance, safety and sustainability standards; adapting to evolving regulations while maintaining operational efficiency is described as an ongoing challenge.

Attracting, developing and retaining skilled talent is a stated key focus area; the BRSR materiality table flags employment as a risk because retaining key talent is vital in manufacturing and higher turnover raises rehiring cost and diminishes morale across a permanent workforce of 1,736 employees as on 31st March 2026.
Safeguarding information systems against cybersecurity risks and ensuring business continuity across manufacturing operations are named as key focus areas within the risk management framework.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety at manufacturing sites
risks.note: The BRSR materiality table flags process-related hazards across sites: inadequate safety procedures or a safety incident would hurt employee health and morale and the Company's reputation, and may cause operational and financial losses including the potential partial shutdown of a plant. Mitigation is a defined safety organisation with EHS policy, objectives and SOPs.

risks.risk: Hazardous waste handling and environmental compliance
risks.note: Hazardous waste generated from high-end equipment requires authorised treatment; waste is sent for disposal to treatment, storage and disposal facilities authorised by the respective SPCB, in compliance with operating permits and hazardous waste authorisations.

one-line thesis: PPAP Automotive marked a strategic inflection point in Q4FY26 via a INR100cr JV divestment and rebranding to 'Ajay Group', driving a 25.7% QoQ revenue recovery to INR174.6cr despite one-off labor code costs. The narrative shifts from pure auto-cyclicality to diversified growth led by a 36% aftermarket surge, imminent battery breakeven, and sharper focus through vertical hiving/mergers.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR174.6cr (Q4, +18.6% YoY, +25.7% QoQ); FY26 Rev: INR567cr. EBITDA: INR16.9cr (+12.9% YoY); Margin ~9.7% (impacted by one-offs). PAT: Impacted by INR3.6cr one-time employee benefit obligation (Labor Code) and mark-to-market investment losses; normalized margins improved to ~13% ex-one-offs. Order Book: INR840cr new business secured in FY26; execution over 3-5 years. Net Debt: Reduced to INR103cr post-divestment proceeds (Gross Debt INR195cr).
guidance: FY27 guidance deferred to Q1FY27 results due to geopolitical/raw material volatility. Implicit targets: Capacity utilization >80-82%; Battery segment PBT profitable; Tooling capacity doubling to ~300 molds/year over 3 years.
order book & pipeline: INR840cr new orders secured in FY26 across EV/ICE; diversified across Maruti, Tata, Mahindra, Honda, Kia, VinFast, Euler Motors; lifetime execution window 3-5 years.
segment / subsidiary detail: Auto Parts: Core revenue driver; new SOPs for SUVs/EVs ramping. Aftermarket: +36% YoY growth; 147 distributors, 1,264 SKUs. Tooling: +12.1% growth; 148 molds developed; >90% utilization. Industrial Products: +38% growth via exports/non-auto. Batteries: Revenue up 1.28x YoY; Q4 loss narrowed to INR40L (vs INR1.2cr prior year); targeting 100% utilization in FY27.
growth verticals / optionality: Aftermarket expansion (25%+ CAGR target); Battery segment turnaround (profitable PBT expected FY27); Tooling scale-up (double capacity); New OEM wins (VinFast, Euler, Kia, Mahindra) shifting portfolio to 90% SUVs.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 EBITDA margin ~9.7% suppressed by INR3.6cr labor code one-off; underlying operational margin ~13%. Raw material inflation ongoing; 50% pass-through achieved, balance under negotiation. Cost mitigation via solar energy adoption and employee reforms planned.
capex / expansion: Future capex to be funded via internal accruals; no immediate debt increase planned. Strategic funds from JV divestment (INR100cr) reserved for M&A or strategic investments, not routine capex.
capital allocation: Divestment proceeds (INR100cr) allocated to strengthen reserves, reduce net debt (to INR103cr), and fund future strategic opportunities. Final dividend INR1.5/share (Total FY26: INR2.5/share).
risks & watch-items: West Asia conflict disrupting logistics and elevating raw material costs. Delayed SOPs from specific OEM models (now resolving). Regulatory delays in subsidiary merger/hive-off approvals. Entry-level sedan demand weakness (mitigated by SUV shift).
management quality / tone: Cautiously Optimistic; Transparent on one-offs; Strategic/Restructuring-focused; Emphasizing operational efficiency and portfolio rebalancing towards high-growth verticals.
non-obvious takeaways: Rebranding to 'Ajay Group' signals a holistic conglomerate strategy beyond just 'PPAP'. The battery unit's rapid loss reduction (INR1.2cr to INR40L in one year) suggests a faster-than-expected turnaround trajectory. 78% of revenue now comes from vehicles <5 years old, reducing obsolescence risk.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material inflation and supply chain disruption from West Asia conflict affecting margins. | Competitors with fixed-price contracts and no pass-through mechanisms | loser | Med | PPAP has secured 50% pass-through immediately, putting competitors without such clauses at a relative disadvantage. |
| Shift in consumer preference from sedans to SUVs rendering old portfolios obsolete. | PPAP Automotive Limited | beneficiary | High | 90% of PPAP's upcoming models are SUVs; 78% of revenue from <5yr old vehicles aligns perfectly with current demand trends. |
| High losses in EV battery startups deterring traditional auto ancillaries. | PPAP Automotive Limited | beneficiary | Med | Near-breakeven status (INR40L loss) and 100% utilization target for FY27 positions PPAP ahead of peers still burning significant cash in battery ventures. |

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: PPAP Automotive Limited is the flagship company of the AJAY Group and a leading manufacturer of automotive body sealing systems, injection-molded plastic components and engineered polymer products for passenger vehicle OEMs, with over four decades of experience in engineering and manufacturing.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: PPAP manufactures automotive body sealing systems, injection-molded plastic components and engineered polymer products for leading passenger vehicle OEMs across India, using plastic extrusion, plastic injection molding, rubber processing and advanced manufacturing technologies. Its components are compatible with both internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric vehicle (EV) platforms, making the portfolio largely engine-agnostic. Around the core automotive parts business the Group has added an aftermarket distribution business (ELPIS), a commercial tooling vertical, an industrial products business (Avinya Industrial Products) and a lithium-ion battery pack business (Avinya Batteries).

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- ELPIS Automotives Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% of shares held by the listed entity (BRSR Section A item 23); listed in Form AOC-1 Part A; related-party counterparty for material / licence purchases, sales and receipts for other services.
- Avinya Batteries Limited (formerly PPAP Technology Limited) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% of shares held; participates in the Business Responsibility initiatives of the listed entity; related-party counterparty for a loan given, loan repayment received and receipts for other services.
- Avinya Industrial Products Limited — subsidiary: Incorporated 29.03.2025. Listed as a wholly owned subsidiary in the related-party note and in Form AOC-1 Part A, but the BRSR Section A item 23 table labels it a Joint Venture while showing 100% of shares held by the listed entity — the two disclosures in this bundle conflict. Related-party counterparty for payment for other services, investment in equity shares, receipts for other services and sales.
- Meraki Precision Tool Engineering Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% of shares held; incorporated 24.03.2025; related-party counterparty for investment in equity shares and payments for other services.
- Avinya Sealing Systems Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary, 100% of shares held; incorporated 21.02.2025; named in Form AOC-1 (as Avinya Sealing Systems Private Limited, CIN U22199DL2025PLC443070) among subsidiaries yet to commence operations; related-party counterparty for investment in equity shares.
- PPAP Tokai India Rubber Private Limited — JV: Joint venture that ceased to be a JV w.e.f. 01.01.2026; shares held at year end, investment amount and extent of holding are all Nil, and it is listed in Form AOC-1 Part B among joint ventures sold during the year (CIN U25112DL2012PTC235036). Significant influence was due to shareholding. Related-party counterparty during the year for material / licence purchases, receipts for other services and sales.
- Vinay and Ajay Jain Foundation — related party: Related party in the group where common control exists; counterparty for CSR expenses paid.
- PPAP Automotive Limited Employees Group Gratuity Fund Trust — related party: Other related party — post-employment benefit plan of the Company; counterparty for the employer's contribution towards the gratuity fund.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Auto Parts: Core revenue driver; new SOPs for SUVs/EVs ramping. Aftermarket: +36% YoY growth; 147 distributors, 1,264 SKUs. Tooling: +12.1% growth; 148 molds developed; >90% utilization. Industrial Products: +38% growth via exports/non-auto. Batteries: Revenue up 1.28x YoY; Q4 loss narrowed to INR40L (vs INR1.2cr prior year); targeting 100% utilization in FY27.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Automotive Parts:** automotive body sealing systems, injection-molded plastic components, engineered polymer products
- **Aftermarket (ELPIS):** engineering plastic components, rubber sealing systems, service parts, vehicle accessories, car care products, perfumes
- **Commercial Tooling:** high-precision plastic injection molds, multi-cavity molds, gas-assisted molds, hot runner systems, 2K moulding and over-moulding
- **Industrial Products:** pail containers, paint dispensers and buckets, components for solar panel cleaning robots, AHU systems, modern bath fittings, white goods components
- **Battery and Energy Storage:** lithium-ion battery packs (pouch, cylindrical and prismatic cell-based), battery packs for solar energy systems, telecom infrastructure, Energy Storage Systems (ESS), inverters and UPS

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Passenger vehicle OEMs in India, across both ICE and EV platforms
- Automotive replacement / aftermarket, B2B and B2C
- Automotive, electrical, white goods and other industrial sectors for precision molds
- Infrastructure, renewable energy, construction, electrical equipment and consumer appliances (industrial products)
- Mobility and stationary energy storage — solar, telecom, ESS, inverters and UPS
- Export markets (industrial products and tooling)

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: INR840cr new orders secured in FY26 across EV/ICE; diversified across Maruti, Tata, Mahindra, Honda, Kia, VinFast, Euler Motors; lifetime execution window 3-5 years.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: FY27 guidance deferred to Q1FY27 results due to geopolitical/raw material volatility. Implicit targets: Capacity utilization >80-82%; Battery segment PBT profitable; Tooling capacity doubling to ~300 molds/year over 3 years.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Aftermarket expansion (25%+ CAGR target); Battery segment turnaround (profitable PBT expected FY27); Tooling scale-up (double capacity); New OEM wins (VinFast, Euler, Kia, Mahindra) shifting portfolio to 90% SUVs.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's auto component industry is expected to grow at a 7-8% CAGR between FY25 and FY30, supported by robust domestic demand, rising exports, favourable policy and technological advancement.
- Record Indian automobile sales in FY26 across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, three-wheelers and two-wheelers, plus record vehicle exports, are expected to support demand for automotive components and related industries.
- Electrification, smartification, premiumization and localization are the key trends driving component demand, with the mix shifting towards high-value products such as battery systems and electric powertrains.
- Government programmes — the PLI Scheme, Make in India, FAME and PM E-Drive — are accelerating EV adoption and domestic manufacturing of advanced automotive components.
- Favourable demographics, rising vehicle ownership and continued growth in domestic manufacturing support a positive long-term industry outlook.
- A growing aftermarket, India's growing vehicle parc and rising average vehicle age underpin demand for replacement parts and accessories.
- Rising premium vehicle penetration supports demand for higher-value sealing, plastic and aesthetic components.
- Management flags geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain disruptions, commodity price volatility and evolving regulatory requirements as the key risks to this demand outlook.
- Automotive parts: secured new business wins worth approximately Rs 840 crore across both EV and ICE vehicle platforms in FY26.
- Automotive parts: new projects started for Tata Motors Sierra, MSIL E Vitara & Victoris and Renault-Nissan Duster, with launch readiness under development for Tata Motors, Mahindra, Honda and Maruti Suzuki programs.
- Tooling: maintained a robust order pipeline across automotive and non-automotive sectors, supporting future growth; the stated priority is to maintain a strong order pipeline to provide sustained revenue visibility.
- Tooling: 148 precision molds developed and delivered in FY26, with capacity utilisation improving to over 90%.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 EBITDA margin ~9.7% suppressed by INR3.6cr labor code one-off; underlying operational margin ~13%. Raw material inflation ongoing; 50% pass-through achieved, balance under negotiation. Cost mitigation via solar energy adoption and employee reforms planned.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Divestment proceeds (INR100cr) allocated to strengthen reserves, reduce net debt (to INR103cr), and fund future strategic opportunities. Final dividend INR1.5/share (Total FY26: INR2.5/share).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: PPAP's stated expansion agenda for the automotive parts business covers work at the Pathredi, Gujarat and Chennai manufacturing facilities to enhance operational efficiency, optimize production flow and improve capacity utilization, together with the set-up of a solar plant for energy efficiency; commissioning of a new EPDM extrusion line and a second mixing line at the new Chennai facility; and expansion of the manufacturing footprint through new facilities at Sambhaji Nagar and Chakan, Pune, to support capacity growth and customer proximity. The product portfolio is to be widened with value-added components to raise content per vehicle. In the aftermarket business (ELPIS Automotives Private Limited) the build-out is distribution-led — a pan-India network supported by regional warehouses, an omnichannel/digital commerce presence and direct exports to the Middle East, Africa and South Asia. The tooling business, run from the Greater Noida facility, is to receive continued investment in high-speed machining, automation and advanced CAD/CAM systems, and is proposed to be transferred into a dedicated wholly owned subsidiary, Meraki Precision Tool Engineering Limited, during FY27 subject to statutory and regulatory approvals. The industrial products business, which has a facility in Surajpur, Uttar Pradesh, established an additional facility at Greater Noida during FY26 to improve customer proximity and delivery responsiveness. In batteries, growth is to be driven through prismatic line capacity expansion, and Avinya Batteries Limited is proposed to be merged into PPAP Automotive Limited, subject to the requisite statutory and regulatory approvals, with the merger expected to complete during FY27. No rupee capex quantum is disclosed in this material: the Capital Commitments and Segment Capital Expenditure named-disclosure blocks arrive with their labels only and carry no attributable figure.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously Optimistic; Transparent on one-offs; Strategic/Restructuring-focused; Emphasizing operational efficiency and portfolio rebalancing towards high-growth verticals.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Over four decades of experience in engineering and manufacturing as the flagship of the AJAY Group
- Engine-agnostic product portfolio compatible with both ICE and EV platforms, making it future-ready
- Manufacturing network located close to major automotive production hubs across Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra, supported by 7 manufacturing facilities at Group level
- Operating scale — daily dispatches exceeding 2.3 lakh parts, over 50 customers and a portfolio of 3000+ SKUs
- Diversified blue-chip customer base including Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors and Honda, with Mahindra & Mahindra onboarded as a direct OEM customer and CIE Golde as a direct Tier-I customer in FY26
- Technical collaboration with Nissen Chemitec Corporation, Japan, and a technology partnership agreement with Hutchinson entered in June 2026 giving access to European body-sealing technology and licensed knowhow
- In-house precision tooling capability (multi-cavity, gas-assisted, hot runner, 2K and over-moulding) supporting new product development
- Core process capabilities spanning plastic extrusion, plastic injection molding and rubber processing, transferable to non-automotive industrial applications

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: West Asia conflict disrupting logistics and elevating raw material costs. Delayed SOPs from specific OEM models (now resolving). Regulatory delays in subsidiary merger/hive-off approvals. Entry-level sedan demand weakness (mitigated by SUV shift).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Rebranding to 'Ajay Group' signals a holistic conglomerate strategy beyond just 'PPAP'. The battery unit's rapid loss reduction (INR1.2cr to INR40L in one year) suggests a faster-than-expected turnaround trajectory. 78% of revenue now comes from vehicles <5 years old, reducing obsolescence risk.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Build the AJAY Group as a diversified enterprise around the automotive parts core, with five companies each addressing a distinct segment of the mobility and industrial value chain — automotive components, aftermarket, industrial products, precision tooling and energy storage.
- Simplify the group structure: complete the divestment of the PPAP Tokai India Rubber Private Limited stake, transfer the tooling business into wholly owned subsidiary Meraki Precision Tool Engineering Limited during FY27, and merge Avinya Batteries Limited into PPAP.
- Keep the automotive product portfolio engine-agnostic …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material inflation and supply chain disruption from West Asia conflict affecting margins. | Competitors with fixed-price contracts and no pass-through mechanisms | loser | Med | PPAP has secured 50% pass-through immediately, putting competitors without such clauses at a relative disadvantage. |
| Shift in consumer preference from sedans to SUVs rendering old portfolios obsolete. | PPAP Automotive Limited | beneficiary | High | 90% of PPAP's upcoming models are SUVs; 78% of revenue from <5yr old vehicles aligns perfectly with current demand trends. |
| High losses in EV battery startups deterring traditional auto ancillaries. | PPAP Automotive Limited | beneficiary | Med | Near-breakeven status (INR40L loss) and 100% utilization target for FY27 positions PPAP ahead of peers still burning significant cash in battery ventures. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [JV exit] The deck records "Approved sale of 50% Stake in PPAP Tokai India Rubber to Tokai Kogyo" in the 2024-2026 milestone block, and footnotes that "PTI ceases to exist as a part of Ajay group by the sale of entire 50% stake in JV company, PPAP Tokai India Rubber". FY26 exceptional items (INR 49.8 Crore consolidated / INR 32.7 Crore standalone) sit in the same year, but the deck does not explicitly link them.
- [Group reorganisation] The group-structure slide marks two reorganisation steps — "Slump Sale of Tooling Business" and "Merger of the Avinya Batteries Business with PPAP Automotive" — alongside the note "Existing Structure Continues" for the other entities. The arrows binding each step to specific entities are not recoverable from the text extract, so no direction is asserted here.
- [Group context] PPAP sits within the AJAY Group (name derived from Sanskrit A + JAY, "the unconquered and the undefeated"), whose disclosed businesses span OEM/OES mobility parts, mobility aftermarket, industrial applications, plastic injection tooling, Li-ion battery packs for mobility and for energy storage, warehousing, a plant nursery, and CSR covering tree plantation, education for the underprivileged and sports.
- [Industry backdrop, SIAM Q1FY27] Passenger vehicle sales grew 25.9% YoY to a record 12.74 lakh units with PV exports up 8.8% to 2.22 lakh units; commercial vehicles hit a record first quarter at 2.65 lakh units (+18.3%) with exports up 43.3% to ~28,000 units; three-wheelers posted a record 3.68 lakh units (+29.7%) with exports up 57.7% to 1.51 lakh units; two-wheeler exports surged 36.6% to a record 1.55 million units.
- [Awards] Customer-conferred recognitions listed include Overall Performance Award and Manufacturing Excellence Award (MSIL), Annual Supplier award (Tata Motors), Outstanding Performance in Quality (Honda), Silver Award for Delivery (HCIL), Best Quality and Quality Upgradation Initiatives (Suzuki), Quality Circle Bronze Award (TKSA), 1st position in Kaizen Competition (Tata) and Best Practice in Digital Transformation (CII).
